CompareFunctionStudy.description: Test preservation across two revisions. Declare the only allowed changed time interval and channel names. Samples the whole composition at <=20ms plus exact event joins. Returns max/RMS errors outside the allowed scope, timestamps, and changed event metadata. Empty allowedChannels means no channel may change. Does not prove absence of hidden narrow features.

CompareRectSLStudy.description: Check what an edit preserved: pixels (mode rgb, or luma for brightness only) held to one level outside allowedRegion [x0,y0,x1,y1] in wall units, and — by id — which rectangles changed (position, size, rotation, opacity, fill, material, order), appeared or went, grouped by the line that made them. Name rectangles so their ids survive edits.

openai.description: Check what an edit preserved: pixels (mode rgb, or luma for brightness only) held to one level outside allowedRegion [x0,y0,x1,y1] in wall units, and — by id — which rectangles changed (position, size, rotation, opacity, fill, material, order), appeared or went, grouped by the line that made them. Name rectangles so their ids survive edits.

CompareStackAutoSlot.description: Check what an edit preserved, in the host shader: each revision is bound live in turn and captured where the module draws, then the slot's own program is put back. mode rgb compares displayed colour, luma brightness only; allowedRegion [u0,v0,u1,v1] (0..1 of the capture, y up) is where change may happen, and outside it everything must stay within one level. A host that animates the slot differs between the two captures by its own motion too.

openai.description: Check what an edit preserved, in the host shader: each revision is bound live in turn and captured where the module draws, then the slot's own program is put back. mode rgb compares displayed colour, luma brightness only; allowedRegion [u0,v0,u1,v1] (0..1 of the capture, y up) is where change may happen, and outside it everything must stay within one level. A host that animates the slot differs between the two captures by its own motion too.

CompareStackSLStudy.description: Check what an edit preserved. mode rgb compares displayed colour, luma brightness only, stage what each program leaves on the stack after beforeStage/afterStage (e.g. to prove a recolour left the field before the palette untouched; for a line ending in a store >name it compares the stored value). allowedRegion [u0,v0,u1,v1] is where change may happen; outside it everything must stay within one level (1e-6 for stage).

EditFunctionStudy.description: Compile, check and activate a COMPLETE Kotlin candidate in this box. Must return StudyComposition of pure Functions.Fn channels. Expected revision AND live source hash from Inspect are required. Failed compile/check keeps the working revision. This is trusted local Kotlin in Field, not a sandbox. Preserve unrelated source and stable event IDs. Returns compilation/check evidence and an actual image preview; this satisfies Kotlin verification for this standalone study. No extra CompileKotlin or Observe call is needed unless a different interval or additional evidence is required. Prefer PatchFunctionStudy for small edits.

source.description: Complete Kotlin source with imports. Last expression returns afield.stdlib.StudyComposition. No filesystem/network/process effects; no mutable or stateful evaluators.

Needs expectedRevision and expectedSourceHash from Inspect; a stale guard or failed check changes nothing. Prefer PatchRectSLStudy or SetRectSLNumbers for small edits.

source.description: Complete RectSL source. Keep it human-editable: scene words first, one object per paragraph with a # comment saying what it is, named rectangles ("sun" rect), : name ... ; definitions for repeated motifs.

EditStackAutoSlot.description: Replace a slot's whole StackSL program. It must compile into this slot (the host shader's own samplers and push constants are fine); it is then bound live, the slot recompiles in place, and it is written back into the box's Kotlin where it sits verbatim. Returns a picture of the result in the host shader — the real end result, or with over a sheet of moments across that many seconds. Needs expectedRevision and expectedSourceHash from Inspect. Prefer PatchStackAutoSlot or SetStackAutoNumbers for small changes.

ExportFunctionStudy.description: Export the checked function revision to CSV files in this document's files directory, using Field's file resolver. One filename per channel, exactly as requested (no automatic .csv suffix). Each row is time in seconds, signal*scale. Includes the exact endpoint; no header by default. Files are staged and verified before publication. Requires the revision source hash; refuses dirty current source. Set overwrite=true only when the user asks to replace/re-export. Returns paths, revision, rows, duration, sample rate and checksums. No generic Kotlin evaluation or further verification is needed.

ExportRectSLStudy.description: Export a checked revision into this document's files directory: kind png (one frame at seconds) or mp4 (the whole clip at the scene's fps, repeated loops times; needs ffmpeg). Runs in the background and returns at once with an estimate, timed from one real frame, and refuses one over maxMinutes with a size that fits; tell the person where the file will appear and how long it should take. Progress is in InspectRectSLStudy's exports. The filename is used literally. Refuses an unchecked editor edit; overwrite only when asked.

maxMinutes.description: Refuse an export estimated to take longer than this many minutes; the refusal names a size that fits. Raise it only if the person agrees to wait

size.description: Pixels along the wall's longer side; 0 means 1920 for png and 1280 for mp4

InspectFunctionStudy.description: Inspect this function study: authoritative Kotlin, stable event IDs, assumptions, selection, revision history and live source hash. Inspect once before editing; when dirty, liveSource is the editable source and source is the checked revision. Reuse the returned hash for the edit. Historical revisions are immutable. Prefer PatchFunctionStudy for local changes.

InspectRectSLStudy.description: Read this RectSL study: the checked scene, whether the editor holds an unchecked human edit (dirty; then liveSource is what is in the box and liveCheck says whether it compiles), revision history, the scene's shape (wall, duration, rectangles, what is visible when), the analysis's warnings, the lines that make rectangles, knobs (typed numbers and colours, one line each: index, line:column, as typed, what reads it), and personAt — the line the person's editor cursor is on, which a click on a rectangle in the window moves to the line that made it, so 'this one' usually means it. Inspect once before editing and reuse liveSourceHash. The window above the box plays the scene live; prefer ObserveRectSLStudy or TimelineRectSLStudy, which draw exact times.

openai.description: Read this RectSL study: the checked scene, whether the editor holds an unchecked human edit (dirty; then liveSource is what is in the box and liveCheck says whether it compiles), revision history, the scene's shape (wall, duration, rectangles, what is visible when), the analysis's warnings, the lines that make rectangles, knobs (typed numbers and colours, one line each: index, line:column, as typed, what reads it), and personAt — the line the person's editor cursor is on, which a click on a rectangle in the window moves to the line that made it, so 'this one' usually means it. Inspect once before editing and reuse liveSourceHash. The window above the box plays the scene live; prefer ObserveRectSLStudy or TimelineRectSLStudy, which draw exact times.

InspectStackAutoSlot.description: Read a stack.auto slot's study: its program, the host shader's lines that declare and call it (what its input and output mean — the host decides, not StackSL's own frame), where the module is drawn (the window, a render target), the compiler's problems and warnings, its numbers (knobs: index, line:column, as typed, the operand the compiler took it as, the card's name in brackets, and whether it is turned live but not kept), keys, and history. slot may be empty when the box has only one. Inspect once before editing and reuse sourceHash.

openai.description: Read a stack.auto slot's study: its program, the host shader's lines that declare and call it (what its input and output mean — the host decides, not StackSL's own frame), where the module is drawn (the window, a render target), the compiler's problems and warnings, its numbers (knobs: index, line:column, as typed, the operand the compiler took it as, the card's name in brackets, and whether it is turned live but not kept), keys, and history. slot may be empty when the box has only one. InspectStackSLStudy.description: Read this StackSL study: the checked program, whether the editor holds an unchecked human edit (dirty; then liveSource is what is in the box and liveCheck says whether it compiles), revision history, compiler warnings, stages (one per line), knobs (the numbers a person typed, one line each: index, line:column, as typed, the operand the compiler took it as — 'mix amount', 'multiply b'), and personAt — the line the person's editor cursor is on, so 'this line' usually means it. Inspect once before editing and reuse liveSourceHash. Historical revisions are immutable. Renders come from the GPU of the window above the program (the CPU reference, slowly, when there is none). The window also shows the program live at whatever time it has reached; prefer ObserveStackSLStudy, which renders exact times. ReloadShaders does not apply: an accepted edit reaches the window by itself.

Overview uses min/max per pixel; request <=25 seconds for resolved waveform. All output describes one immutable revision. Images are sent to the model as image inputs. For preservation, compare intervals outside the union of old/new event supports.

Do not call CompileKotlin again. Choose a preview interval around the changed signal; default is the first 25 seconds.

TimelineRectSLStudy.description: See the whole clip at once: frames evenly across the duration, and a chart of how many rectangles are visible, how much of the wall they cover and how fast they move, with the events a viewer would notice (a rectangle entering or leaving the wall, stopping, starting, turning, fading, touching another), each named with the line that made it. Use it to judge pacing and to find the moment something goes wrong.

Use it to judge pacing and to find the moment something goes wrong.

TraceRectSLStudy.description: Find which line made what. mode identify draws the frame at seconds with every visible rectangle outlined in its line's colour and labelled L<line>, and lists the lines with example rectangles (centre, size, fill); use it to answer 'which of these is the one on line 12?' or 'what is that shape?'. mode build shows the scene after each line that makes something. Give probeX and probeY (a wall point) to also get everything covering that point at seconds, topmost first, with the line that made each — the way to answer 'what is this, and why is it here?'.

probeX.description: x of a wall point to probe, in wall units (the frame's convention); omit for none

probeY.description: y of a wall point to probe, in wall units; omit for none

TraceStackSLStudy.description: Read the program as pictures: what each stage (line, or word for a one-line program) leaves on top of the stack — for a line ending in a store (>name), the value it stored — with value ranges and stack depth. Set probeU and probeV (0..1) to also get the top four stack values at that point after every root word — the way to answer 'why is this pixel black?'.

probeU.description: uv x of a point to probe, 0..1; negative for none

probeV.description: uv y of a point to probe, 0..1 with y up; negative for none

TryRectSLVariants.description: Speculate: check and draw 1..8 candidate scenes beside the current one without publishing. Each variant is a complete source or exact edits to the live source, with a short label and note. They are held so the person can Adopt one in the study card, or you can with AdoptRectSLVariant. Labels are short (A, B or 'drift').

TryStackAutoVariants.description: Speculate in the host shader: check 1..8 candidate programs for a slot, bind each live in turn and capture it where the module draws, then put the slot's own program back. Nothing is kept or written into the code. Each is a complete source or exact edits, with a short label (A, B or 'ember') and note; they are held for AdoptStackAutoVariant.
